reasoning_content:
ddev works as the dev user. Next let's try starting the project. The config.yaml specifies mysql 8.0, PHP 8.4. Let's run `ddev start` in /workspace as the dev user.

Note: the pre-start hook runs `exec-host` to create directories under web/sites/default/... but — wait, `web/` doesn't exist yet! docroot is `web`. composer install will scaffold it. The hook is as follows:
```
exec-host: if [[ ! -d web/sites/default/files/private ]];then mkdir -p web/sites/default/files/private;fi
```
This will create web/sites/default/files/private — mkdir -p works. Next:
```
exec-host: if [[ ! -d web/sites/default/files/translations ]];then mkdir web/sites/default/files/translations;fi
```
This is also fine.
```
exec-host: if [[ ! -h web/sites/default/settings.php ]];then cd web/sites/default/ && ln -sf ../../../.ddev/settings.php;fi
```
This creates the settings.php symlink. Note that since we're root, these get executed as the dev user (exec-host runs on the host). After chown, the dev user owns /workspace, so it's fine.

Alright, let's start the project. `ddev start` pulls the images — could take a while (several hundred MB to download). Let's set a timeout and run it. The terminal's 600-second timeout applies per command. First run `ddev start`, and if it times out, check the state and continue.
